title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: INSPIRE PROGRAMME
body_text:
Over the last five years, the Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research (INSPIRE) Programme of the department of science and technology has systematically nurtured scientific talent at different stages of the academic and research pipeline through its four major components. INSPIRE MANAK (Million Minds Augmenting National Aspiration and Knowledge) promotes innovation and scientific creativity among students aged 10-17 years (Classes VI-XII) by encouraging them to develop and showcase original ideas and innovations. INSPIRE Scholarship for Higher Education (SHE) supports meritorious students aged 17-22 years pursuing undergraduate and postgraduate studies in natural and basic sciences by awarding 12,000 scholarships annually, each valued at ₹80,000 per year. INSPIRE Fellowship encourages outstanding graduates and INSPIRE scholars to pursue research through full-time Ph.D. programme(s) by providing financial support up to five years, including a fellowship of ₹37,000 per month as Junior Research Fellow (JRF), ₹42,000 per month as Senior Research Fellow (SRF), admissible House Rent Allowance (HRA), and an annual contingency grant of ₹20,000. INSPIRE Faculty Fellowship supports outstanding postdoctoral researchers, generally in the 27-32 years age group (with applicable age relaxations for reserved categories), through a five-year fellowship. Fellows receive ₹1,25,000 per month, an annual increment of ₹2,000, and a research grant of ₹35 lakh over the fellowship period.
The Government has been committed to promotion of the Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research (INSPIRE) Programme to encourage meritorious students to pursue higher education and research in science. The component-wise INSPIRE activities during the last five years, including the number of students and young researchers supported under each component, are provided below:
Program/Financial Year 2021-22 2022-23 2023-24 2024-25 2025-26 INSPIRE-MANAK 52720 43381 46926 50009 49805 INSPIRE-SHE 18039 19771 18236 20354 24276 INSPIRE Fellowship 2768 2872 2811 2448 3364 INSPIRE Faculty Fellowship 474 338 299 225 477
With a goal to enhance innovative research by the young generation in the country, impact of these components is being monitored and analysed to facilitate their strategic planning.
The Government has undertaken a series of targeted interventions to significantly expand the outreach and inclusivity of INSPIRE Programme, with a special focus on rural, remote and aspirational districts across the country. These efforts include extensively deep dissemination of information through State Education Departments, District Education Officers, schools and digital platforms; organization of awareness campaigns, orientation programmes, webinars, and capacity-building workshops for teachers and school authorities to improve the quality and reach of nominations; and the conduct of District, State, and National Level Exhibition and Project Competitions (DLEPCs, SLEPCs, and NLEPCs) to identify, recognize and nurture innovative ideas among school students. To further strengthen the innovation ecosystem, mentorship programmes have been organized in collaboration with premier institutions such as IITs, NITs, IISERs, and other leading scientific organizations, providing selected students with guidance on prototype development, innovation, and scientific research. These sustained efforts have led to inclusive participation in the INSPIRE programmes spanning various regions across the country, sections of our society.
A growing number of students from rural and remote districts have benefited through innovation grants, mentoring support, and opportunities to showcase their scientific talent on national platforms. Collectively, these interventions have strengthened the scientific temper and culture of inquiry, fostered grassroots innovation, expanded equitable access to science education, scholarships and research fellowships and broadened the pipeline of young scientific talent from most regions of the country.
This information was given by the Minister of State (Ind. Charge) Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State PMO; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions; Department of Atomic Energy and Space Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

NKR/FT

enrichment.summary: A written Rajya Sabha reply by MoS Dr. Jitendra Singh detailed the DST's INSPIRE Programme, which nurtures scientific talent through four components: MANAK (school students aged 10-17), SHE (undergraduate/postgraduate scholarships), Fellowship (Ph.D. support), and Faculty Fellowship (postdoctoral researchers). Five-year data (2021-22 to 2025-26) shows tens of thousands supported annually across these components, alongside targeted outreach efforts to improve inclusion of rural, remote and aspirational districts.
enrichment.context:
INSPIRE (Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research) is a flagship Department of Science and Technology scheme aimed at attracting talented youth to study science and pursue research careers, addressing India's need to build a robust scientific manpower base and improve its research output. It operates across the entire academic pipeline—from school-level innovation (MANAK) to undergraduate/postgraduate scholarships (SHE), doctoral fellowships (INSPIRE Fellowship), and postdoctoral faculty positions (Faculty Fellowship)—making it one of the few government programmes offering end-to-end support for a scientific career.

The scheme is significant in the context of India's low Gross Expenditure on R&D as a percentage of GDP and concerns over brain drain of scientific talent. By providing structured financial incentives at each stage and through mentorship tie-ups with IITs, NITs, and IISERs, the government aims to build a sustainable talent pipeline and improve scientific temper, particularly in underrepresented rural and aspirational districts. This aligns with broader national goals such as the National Education Policy 2020's emphasis on research and innovation, and the government's push for self-reliance in science and technology (Atal Innovation Mission, Anusandhan National Research Foundation, etc.).

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following components of the INSPIRE Programme specifically targets school students in the age group of 10-17 years?
prelims_questions.explanation: INSPIRE-MANAK (Million Minds Augmenting National Aspiration and Knowledge) promotes innovation among students aged 10-17 years (Classes VI-XII).

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of talent-nurturing programmes like INSPIRE in building India's scientific research ecosystem. What structural challenges remain in translating early innovation into sustained research careers?
Examine the role of targeted outreach and inclusivity measures in government scholarship schemes in bridging the rural-urban divide in access to science education and research opportunities.
